title: Challenge: persist data with volumes and bind mounts
intro: A container's writable layer dies with the container. Volumes and bind mounts keep data alive. Create a volume, mount it, map a host folder, and see where the bytes really live. (Commands are checked, not executed.)

steps.instruction: List the volumes to confirm it exists.
Run a detached container named 'keeper' that mounts 'appdata' at /data.
steps.success:
8a1b2c3d4e5f...
anything written under /data now survives the container being removed
steps.hint: docker run -d --name keeper -v appdata:/data alpine sleep 1d

steps.instruction: Now a bind mount: run a container mapping a host path (e.g. your current directory) into the container.
steps.success:
total 8
-rw-r--r--    1 root     root           42 Jun 24 10:00 README.md
your host files, live, inside the container
steps.fail: Bind-mount a host path: docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/src <image> ls /src

steps.instruction: Inspect the 'appdata' volume to see where Docker stores it on the host.

done: Solved! A named volume (-v appdata:/data) is managed by Docker and survives container removal; a bind mount (-v /host/path:/dir) maps a real host folder straight in. Volumes for app data, bind mounts for code and config.
